answer: A strong sybil defense is proof of useful work tied to a durable reputation graph: each agent must build an atlas of verifiable task history before it can transact at scale, so a new identity starts with near-zero trust. Like saffron, genuine reputation is expensive to grow and easy to lose, while the ripple of a single bad attestation spreads through the graph and devalues every sockpuppet linked to it. Forging thousands of fresh identities then costs far more than any reward they could extract.
